# Match Finder [theUltimator5]

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** analysis-tool. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Match Finder searches a chosen comparison list for the asset whose recent price shape most closely tracks the active chart. It is explicitly about current compatibility, not forecasting continued correlation. After selecting the strongest positive Pearson relationship, it rescales the matched segment for visual comparison, optionally displaying every candidate’s coefficient.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Pearson table/strongest-positive match is independently defined by the disclosed procedure; other missing outputs do not qualify.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Calculate rolling Pearson correlation between chart and comparison ticker segments, excluding self matches, then choose the highest positive correlation.
- Overlay the selected segment with min-max scaling or endpoint-matching rotation and optionally list correlations in a table.
- Over caller N compute r=sum((x-mean(x))*(y-mean(y)))/sqrt(sum((x-mean(x))^2)*sum((y-mean(y))^2)). Exclude self;select largest finite positive r. All-negative,constant/missing series and optional rotation excluded.

## Outputs and intended use

- Inspect which asset/sector has recently tracked the chart; treat the rotated display as adjusted geometry rather than an untouched price series.
- Usable scope: Pearson table/strongest-positive match. Other advertised outputs remain subject to the listed missing information.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Forty ticker slots default broadly to ETFs. Correlation length defaults to 30 with range 10–500; table is initially off and best-fit line yellow.

## Failure modes and caveats

- The source warns of memory/load/timeouts; analytical: selecting the maximum among many correlated assets inflates apparent fit, and rotation forces additional visual agreement.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Handling of all-negative/missing correlations, exact rotation equation, feed alignment and default full ETF set are absent.

## Data requirements

Required inputs: chart and caller-selected comparison closing-price histories.

Repository input-class support: available. Ordinary historical OHLCV/price inputs for caller-selected symbols are a supported data class. Exact selected-symbol cache coverage, synchronization and adjustments remain unverified; no dynamic point-in-time universe is required by the source.

## Idea and objective

Average Lines constructs a moving reference from projections of relationships among historical pivots. Rather than averaging prices directly, it draws a line from the latest pivot to each preceding pivot, extends those lines, and averages their values on subsequent bars. The aim is a new moving-average-like view that incorporates many pivot slopes. The future extensions are geometric extrapolations, not forecasts with established predictive accuracy. The author also uses the script to demonstrate line fills and last-bar indexing, but its pivot-based price reference gives it a financial purpose.

- At a pivot, connect the latest pivot to each earlier pivot and extend the resulting lines.
- On following bars, add the projected line values and average them into a composite reference.

# (Quartile Vol.; Vol. Aggregation; Range US Bars; Gaps) [Kioseff]

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** analysis-tool. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Compare volume distributions, alternative bar aggregations and persistent gaps in one price-action research tool. The publication provides descriptive statistics and chart transformations rather than a complete entry/exit strategy.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Manual cumulative-volume threshold events is independently defined by the disclosed procedure; other missing outputs do not qualify.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Volume quartiles and a high-percentile threshold categorize bars, display dispersions and measure subsequent returns. Successive high-volume observations can receive a regression channel, and a time anchor can start VWAP.
- Range US bars form after separate trend/reversal price thresholds, with state-dependent continuation rules. They use minute OHLC, so multiple reversals within a minute collapse into an approximation.
- Volume-aggregation bars form when cumulative chart-timeframe volume reaches a threshold, carrying excess forward. Gap tracking records partial fills, completion delays and directional statistics, sorting unfilled gaps by price distance.
- Accumulate supplied chart-bar volume against caller positive threshold Q. Mark a threshold event when cumulative volume reaches/exceeds Q;carry the remainder forward. Event timing occurs at observed chart bars,not synthetic tick fills. Multiple events/overshoot price mapping,automatic thresholds,range/gap/quartile outputs remain unqualified.

## Outputs and intended use

- Quartile colors/labels, statistics tables, synthetic bars, gap boxes/lists and anchored VWAP support discretionary analysis.
- Remote gaps can be hidden then reappear when price returns nearby; visibility is distinct from gap validity.
- Usable scope: Manual cumulative-volume threshold events. Other advertised outputs remain subject to the listed missing information.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Automatic or manual range trend/reversal thresholds and volume threshold; date segmentation, forward-return horizon and log-return option.
- Volume includes a 90th-percentile category. Gap minimum size and hide-distance percentage are user settings; warning messages flag overly fine aggregation thresholds.

## Failure modes and caveats

- OHLC approximations cannot recreate tick-level range or volume bars. Small thresholds can produce misleading synthetic structure.
- Conditional returns following high volume are descriptive and sensitive to sample overlap and regime; they do not prove a tradable edge.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Quantile window/interpolation, automatic threshold formulas, gap endpoint definition, intrabar sequencing and precise return-sampling rules are absent.

## Data requirements

Required inputs: ohlcv.

Intraday Volume Swings records price extremes reached during stretches of rising volume, then carries the day’s final selected high and low into the following session. # Risk-Adjusted Momentum Oscillator

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** indicator. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Dampen momentum according to a drawdown-based risk context, then combine normalization, adaptive smoothing and leading-style components. RAMO aims to make momentum signals risk-aware; its broad literature claims do not establish the indicator’s own empirical advantages.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Partly disclosed computation.** Drawdown source/window, normalization order, volatility definition, parameter defaults and exact layered signal conditions are unspecified.

- Drawdown source/window, normalization order, volatility definition, parameter defaults and exact layered signal conditions are unspecified.

## How it works

- Raw momentum may be rate of change, absolute difference or log return. A factor equal to one minus scaled current/max drawdown multiplies momentum, floored to retain a small fraction.
- Z-score normalization clips extreme values. Volatility percentile interpolates EMA alpha, while mean/standard-deviation bands create adaptive thresholds.
- Auxiliary components include EMA-smoothed lagged momentum difference, forward linear-regression extrapolation and an exhaustion flag combining extreme momentum with below-average volume. Crossovers, risk regime and these components inform signal interpretation.

## Outputs and intended use

- Oscillator/signal crosses, risk state, divergence and exhaustion context are described for discretionary confirmation.
- The prose claims automatic position reduction but provides only signal damping equations; an actual portfolio sizing rule cannot be inferred.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Risk factor floor 0.05; normalized scores clipped at ±3.5. Exhaustion volume reference uses 20 bars and volatility percentile 100 observations.
- Risk regimes divide current/max drawdown at 30% and 70%; scaling, lengths, thresholds and alpha bounds are not given concrete defaults.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Zero maximum drawdown requires a guard. Clipping and damping alter amplitude and can delay or suppress valid momentum.
- The stated acceleration is a lagged first difference of momentum, despite the prose calling it a second derivative. Prediction extrapolation does not guarantee leading accuracy.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Drawdown source/window, normalization order, volatility definition, parameter defaults and exact layered signal conditions are unspecified.

# Dynamic Gap Probability Tool

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** analysis-tool. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Dynamic Gap Probability Tool estimates the historical next-candle color associated with the current percentage distance from a selected moving average. It tries to avoid presenting a tiny exact-match sample as reliable by broadening the deviation sample when occurrences are scarce. The table is an empirical conditional-frequency summary, not a calibrated forecast or a rule that resolves whether the trader should favor reversal or continuation.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

**Partly disclosed computation.** Exact-bucket versus cumulative tail counting and deduplication are ambiguous in the principal probability estimator.

- Exact-bucket versus cumulative tail counting and deduplication are ambiguous in the principal probability estimator.

## How it works

- Compute percentage gap as close minus moving average divided by the average, then round its absolute size to the nearest percent.
- Count historical deviations on the corresponding side, expand toward more extreme gap buckets when needed, and estimate the next candle’s green/red proportions.

## Outputs and intended use

- Read current gap, sample size and next-candle green/red percentages together; assess reliability before using the result in another strategy.

## Parameters and stated settings

- MA choices include SMA, EMA, WMA, VWMA, HMA, SMMA and TMA. MA period defaults to 200 and minimum occurrences to 50.
- The example broadens an 8% below-average sample toward 9% and 10% gaps; table position/style are adjustable.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Historical probabilities do not guarantee future outcomes; analytical: overlapping threshold counts and retrospective sample expansion may affect independence and interpretation.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- The prose alternates exact buckets and cumulative inequality counts without explaining deduplication; historical window, doji treatment and causal updating need clarification.

# Market Manipulation Index (MMI)

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** indicator. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Market Manipulation Index is described internally as Composite Manipulation Index, a contextual measure of price orderliness. It combines deviation from a synthetic cycle with error in a short-lag predictive model. The goal is to distinguish structured conditions from unstable conditions before choosing a strategy style. Neither component directly observes manipulative trading, so the manipulation label should not be treated as evidence about participant intent.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Partly disclosed computation.** Sine fitting and ATR-adaptive normalization/smoothing equations are absent.

- Sine fitting and ATR-adaptive normalization/smoothing equations are absent.

## How it works

- Compare actual prices with a user-period sine wave and normalize fitting error by price variance.
- Estimate current price from two lagged closes in rolling linear regression and normalize its error by variance.
- Adapt smoothing windows using ATR, expanding during higher volatility, average the component scores and optionally smooth again.

## Outputs and intended use

- Use low values as the author’s structured-market context, high values as unstable-market context and the middle range as a caution zone.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Output is described as 0–1. Suggested thresholds are below 0.3 and above 0.7, with 0.3–0.7 transitional. Regression inputs are close[1] and close[2].

## Failure modes and caveats

- Analytical: sine mismatch or forecast error can reflect ordinary trends, shocks or model misspecification rather than manipulation.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Sine amplitude/phase fitting, adaptive-window formula, variance handling, clipping and defaults are not disclosed.

## Data requirements

Required inputs: ohlcv.

Fair Value Bands estimates typical price excursions from a selected smooth basis using pivot deviations rather than continuously varying standard deviation. - Inspect threshold retests for trend context or extreme deviations plus price exhaustion for mean-reversion research; configure band/trend alerts.

# Delta Volume Columns Pro [LucF]

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** indicator. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Inspect estimated directional volume through five balance models, with configurable columns, signal lines, divergence context and alerts. Crucially, the publication uses different historical and realtime methods and explicitly warns that refreshed elapsed realtime bars change.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Historical directional-volume raw/EMA balances is independently defined by the disclosed procedure; other missing outputs do not qualify.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Historically, classify lower-timeframe bars into buy/sell bins by direction, carrying the last polarity when unchanged. Realtime mode instead accumulates price/volume feed updates; initial existing bar volume is assigned by current polarity.
- On-bar balance is buy minus sell; average balance subtracts their EMAs. Momentum balance contrasts each EMA with a double-length SMA and applies centered RSI to the directional difference. Relative balance takes positive excesses above separate EMAs, subtracts them and ALMA-smooths; percent balance smooths delta divided by total volume.
- Combined balances sum directional states. Marker bias accumulates signed events; divergence levels retain and expand signal levels on disagreement with bar polarity, leaving subsequent movement to establish direction.
- For supplied historical LTF bars sign volume by candle direction,carrying last polarity when unchanged. U,D are summed directional volumes;OnBar=U-D;Average=EMA(U,n)-EMA(D,n) with caller n/LTF. This historical branch is reproducible independently of live update/reset behavior,ALMA/marker settings and initial-polarity policy;retain data_available=false for full realtime parity and all repaint warnings.

## Outputs and intended use

- Stacked buy/sell columns or a selected balance/bias line, independent coloring/fills, divergence channels and chart-bar colors support discretionary context.
- Markers cover balance agreement, consecutive directional bumps, divergence confirmation and state/bias shifts. The author stresses uncertainty rather than predicting reversals from divergences alone.
- Usable scope: Historical directional-volume raw/EMA balances. Other advertised outputs remain subject to the listed missing information.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Separate smoothing periods, historical intrabar auto/fixed choices, signal/display/marker selection and volume-discrepancy threshold. Default historical targeting uses at least50 intrabars per chart bar.
- Combined state range is -5 to+5; momentum RSI is centered on -50/+50.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Refresh/re-execution repaints elapsed realtime bars and confirmed alerts because they recalculate through the coarser historical model. Live update history cannot be reconstructed from generic candles.
- Volume feeds differ across resolutions and instruments. Legacy platform restrictions in the description are historical claims, not current API guarantees.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Exact period defaults, ALMA settings, historical intrabar extraction implementation and realtime update-volume/reset behavior are not fully specified.

## Data requirements

Required inputs: lower-timeframe OHLCV for historical mode, live incremental price volume feed updates for realtime parity.

# TASC 2026.09 Adaptive SuperSmoother

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** indicator. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Adaptive SuperSmoother adjusts a filter’s critical period according to movement in a fixed-period companion filter. It aims to retain high-frequency noise suppression while responding faster to changing market direction. The adaptive line is compared with the fixed line, and their difference is displayed separately. Ehlers’s suggested directional interpretation is long when adaptive is above fixed and short otherwise, with difference peaks/valleys as possible turning-point clues. Those suggestions are signal concepts rather than a full executable strategy with fills and risk controls.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

**Partly disclosed computation.** The complete filter recurrence and adaptive-period normalization are not supplied.

- The complete filter recurrence and adaptive-period normalization are not supplied.

## How it works

- Filter the source with a fixed-period SuperSmoother, then compute its one-bar change and rolling RMS.
- Scale change by RMS and cap the scaled value; square one minus half that value to derive a period factor.
- Multiply the base period by the factor, enforce a minimum, and run a second SuperSmoother with that adaptive period.

## Outputs and intended use

- Red fixed and blue adaptive lines plus a difference oscillator support directional comparison.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Defaults: Close source, base period 20 and RMS length 81.
- Scaled ROC is capped at 2 and adaptive period floored at 2.

## Failure modes and caveats

- The source does not clarify signed-versus-absolute ROC treatment, materially affecting the period factor.
- Filter crossings can whipsaw and do not establish profitable execution.

**Classification:** financial-library. Native publication type: library. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Deeptest extends strategy reporting with trade statistics, risk-adjusted metrics, drawdowns, distribution diagnostics, benchmark comparison and robustness-style summaries. It reads closed trades from an existing Pine strategy, so it evaluates supplied simulated outcomes rather than creating a strategy. The documentation includes many heuristic quality labels; those labels are not statistical guarantees and its screenshots are explicitly illustrative.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Supplied-equity and closed-trade basic metrics is independently defined by the disclosed procedure; other missing outputs do not qualify.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Extract closed-trade returns and compute profitability, holding-time, exposure, return-distribution and equity-risk summaries; fetch a benchmark for comparison.
- Shuffle historical trade order for Monte Carlo equity scenarios and partition trades into rolling in/out-of-sample segments for comparisons.
- Calculate at last confirmed historical state and render main/complementary tables with tooltips and stress/period cards.
- NetProfit%=100*(FinalEquity-InitialCapital)/InitialCapital. CAGR=(Final/Initial)^(365.25/Days)-1. Payoff=AverageWin/AverageLoss per source sign convention;ProfitFactor=GrossProfit/GrossLoss using absolute totals. Win/BE/Loss rates=count in each class/total trades,shown as percentages;breakeven win%=100/(1+Payoff). Require positive capital/duration,nonzero loss denominators and supplied completed trades. WFA/MC/Sharpe/RoR remain excluded.

## Outputs and intended use

- Import and call runDeeptest in an existing strategy, then assess metric consistency and assumptions rather than relying on a single colored threshold.
- Usable scope: Supplied-equity and closed-trade basic metrics. Other advertised outputs remain subject to the listed missing information.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Source claims more than 112 calculations and over 1,000 shuffle iterations; WFA defaults to twelve windows with roughly 75% in-sample/25% out-of-sample.
- Basic metrics need at least one closed trade; the source suggests thirty-plus for statistical analysis, which is a heuristic rather than universal sufficiency.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Analytical: shuffling unchanged proportional returns does not change compounded terminal wealth without additional path-dependent assumptions; partitioning already-selected trades is not independent parameter retraining.
- The prose includes inconsistent MAR sign language and overstates p-value/alpha interpretations; no-retraining OOS labels require caution.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Trade-return basis, path-dependent sizing, full WFA training procedure, risk-of-ruin assumptions, risk-free rate and all metric implementation details are not supplied.

## Data requirements

Required inputs: caller strategy closed-trade/equity history, S&P 500 benchmark history.

## Idea and objective

Makit0 Volume Profile plots session value references for discretionary stock/futures analysis, originally motivated by regular-session ES levels. It aims to show where session volume concentrated and to retain key auction references on the chart. Its value area surrounds the most heavily traded region, while session extremes and midpoint provide broader context. Crucially, the author says this implementation uses the current chart’s candles rather than finer intrabar data. Therefore its profile is resolution-dependent and should not be assumed to match a built-in tick- or lower-timeframe profile.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Independent session-range output: within the chosen CT session, track the maximum chart-bar high and minimum chart-bar low and draw HIGH, LOW and their midpoint (HIGH+LOW)/2. Use chart resolution compatible with session boundaries; these lines do not depend on volume allocation, POC or value-area calculations.
- Allocate session candle volume across price levels, identify maximum-volume POC and determine the value-area boundaries.
- Compute session high, low and midpoint and optionally extend all reference lines.
- Restrict processing/display to supported minute charts and selected session hours.

## Outputs and intended use

- POC, VAH/VAL and high/low/mid lines plus optional out-of-session shading support auction-context analysis.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Value area contains 70% of session volume. Supported minutes are 1,2,3,5,10,15,30.
- Sessions: RTH 08:30–15:15 CT default; GLOBEX 17:00–08:30; FULL 17:00–15:15.
- History defaults to one 12-hour period; levels/shading default on and line extension off.
- Narrow session-range scope uses RTH 08:30–15:15 CT (default), GLOBEX 17:00–08:30 CT, or FULL 17:00–15:15 CT; Show Range defaults true. MID is the range midpoint, not volume-weighted value.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Coarser chart resolution changes estimated price-volume distribution.
- Session definitions and daylight-saving alignment must match the instrument; many extended levels can obscure charts.

# Logarithmic Moving Average (LMA) [QuantAlgo]

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** indicator. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Logarithmic Moving Average converts a logarithmically weighted price average into a trend-quality-adjusted slope oscillator. Its aim is to favor recent data while distinguishing cleaner directional movement from weaker drift. Optional log-return momentum further amplifies agreement; this is a designed weighting rule rather than evidence of statistical significance or higher continuation probability.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** LMA/ten-bar slope is independently defined by the disclosed procedure; other missing outputs do not qualify.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Weight closing prices by inverse squared log of age plus steepness, normalize into an average and measure its percentage slope over a fixed lag.
- Multiply slope by a half-base/half-R-squared trend-quality factor; optionally apply a same-direction momentum multiplier.
- For ages i=0..N-1,w_i=1/log(i+steepness)^2;LMA=sum(w_i*close[i])/sum(w_i). Require i+steepness>0 and not1. Slope=100*(LMA-LMA[10])/LMA[10] for nonzero lagged value. Final quality/momentum/smoothing excluded.

## Outputs and intended use

- Positive/negative values convey bullish/bearish momentum, zero crosses suggest regime transitions and threshold zones flag stronger readings; gradient/bar colors and latest classification aid inspection.
- Usable scope: LMA/ten-bar slope. Other advertised outputs remain subject to the listed missing information.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Slope uses a ten-bar lag. Long/short thresholds default +0.5/-0.5; source calls ±1 strong extremes. Period, steepness, smoothing and momentum controls lack full defaults.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Analytical: log weights need valid domain/normalization, trend-quality weighting is not calibrated predictive confidence, and optional amplification changes scale.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- R-squared calculation window, steepness bounds, momentum annualization/multiplier, smoothing and full defaults are not fully disclosed.

# NeuraLib: A Native AI and Deep Learning Runtime

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** financial-library. Native publication type: library. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Provide a native neural-network research runtime for financial indicators and strategies. NeuraLib packages tensor operations, automatic differentiation, training, validation and scaling, leaving the caller to define a model, target and trading interpretation.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Partly disclosed computation.** The financial runtime API and example workflow are extensive, but core tensor/training and custom-loss behavior remains undisclosed for an independent reproduction.

- Tensor/gradient kernels, initializer defaults, optimizer constants, custom finance-loss equations and scaler/split edge rules are not reproduced in the description.

## How it works

- A sequential builder assembles input, dense, activation, dropout and normalization blocks; custom computational graphs extend it with matrix, sequence and attention primitives. Forward evaluation produces tensors; backward propagation accumulates gradients and optimizer steps update parameters.
- Window/rolling datasets validate row widths and missing values, preserve chronology, separate training and holdout batches, and scale validation using a training-side profile. Prediction outputs can be inverse-scaled into target units.
- Training may run only at the confirmed historical edge or on every explicit call. Optimizer schedules, clipping, accumulation and early stopping control updates. Dropout Monte Carlo prediction returns mean/variance, not a calibrated financial risk distribution.

## Outputs and intended use

- APIs return tensors, predictions, loss/metric history and serialized weights. The first example explicitly plots an untrained model; the return example pairs previous-bar RSI/EMA-relative price/ATR fraction/momentum with a matured next return.
- Companion model extensions add recurrent/convolutional/attention blocks and replay utilities. These capabilities do not establish profitable forecasts or implementation parity.

## Parameters and stated settings

- The return example uses four features, eight hidden units, dropout0.10, AdamW learning rate0.003, a500-row dataset, readiness64 and a16-row validation holdout; trainBatch(16) returns the training side of that split, not a16-row training batch.
- Model dimensions, RNG seed, loss/metrics, scaler kinds, optimizer constants, training gate/cadence and schedules are caller choices.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Claimed external-runtime parity and leakage guards are author assertions without supporting tests in this description. Full-history repeated fitting can still contaminate model-selection judgments if validation is reused.

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** indicator. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

AutoTune Filter estimates a dominant cycle from negative autocorrelation of high-pass-filtered data and uses that estimate to tune a bandpass filter. It aims to preserve cycle alignment while avoiding abrupt center-period changes. The author proposes turning-point context from the tuned filter’s rate of change, but cycle structure in recent data does not guarantee the next market oscillation.

- Highpass and bandpass recursions/bandwidth, ACF estimator/window endpoints, initialization and window default are not provided.

## How it works

- Apply a two-pole highpass filter, calculate rolling autocorrelation over the cutoff/window length and choose the smallest lag attaining minimum correlation.
- Double that lag for candidate cycle length, limit per-bar period movement and use the result as a bandpass center.

## Outputs and intended use

- Display highpass data, minimum correlation, dominant cycle or final tuned bandpass; a zero derivative with positive/negative filter sign is proposed as local-high/low context.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Cycle estimate is twice selected lag and period change is capped at two per bar. Four output modes exist, with tuned bandpass default; Window controls ACF/cutoff.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Analytical: autocorrelation minima can be unstable in nonstationary data and an apparent half-cycle can reflect noise rather than persistent periodicity.

# Trend Line Methods (TLM)

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** drawing-tool. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Trend Line Methods draws two complementary channel estimates: one connects stored pivots, while the other fits boundaries through segment extremes over a fixed window. It supports discretionary structure analysis and explicitly provides neither trade signals nor risk management. Agreement between the channels is proposed as a reference zone, not independent statistical confirmation of support or resistance.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Confirmed-pivot span channel is independently defined by the disclosed procedure; other missing outputs do not qualify.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- For Pivot Span, connect oldest/latest stored pivot highs for the upper line and corresponding lows for the lower line.
- For the straight channel, divide a window into five segments, select each segment’s highest high/lowest low and fit separate regression-style lines through those representatives.
- With caller left/right pivot confirmation/count window,retain confirmed highs/lows. For each side connect oldest retained pivot(t0,p0) to latest(t1,p1):line(t)=p0+(p1-p0)*(t-t0)/(t1-t0). Require two distinct timestamps;caller defines ties. Update only when newly confirmed pivots enter. Five-point regression/style extras excluded.

## Outputs and intended use

- Compare recent-swing and broader-window boundaries and optional fill for planning within an existing trading process.
- Usable scope: Confirmed-pivot span channel. Other advertised outputs remain subject to the listed missing information.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Method toggles, pivot left/right counts, retained count, lookback/channel length, line style/thickness and colors are configurable; second method uses five segments.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Analytical: confirmed pivots lag, segment boundaries affect fitted slopes and the two methods share price data rather than provide independent evidence.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

# Delta Volume Candles [LucF]

Version: 1.0.0. Delta: individual explanation of the complete saved publication.

**Classification:** indicator. Native publication type: study. Review: independently reviewed.

## Idea and objective

Delta Volume Candles augments or replaces price candles with intrabar-derived volume-pressure information. It separates up/down intrabar volume, constructs several balance measures and uses them for candle additions, moving-average channels, divergence regions, colors and configurable alerts. The author presents delta as a proxy for participation convergence with price, explicitly warning against rigid reversal inference from declining delta.

## Coin-test readiness: incomplete

No complete standalone coin-test contract or runnable coin-test implementation has been qualified for this card. Source disclosure alone does not establish that readiness.

## Source calculation and gaps

**Disclosed principal calculation.** Historical raw/EMA directional-volume balances is independently defined by the disclosed procedure; other missing outputs do not qualify.

No blocking gap was identified for the principal computation described above. Runtime integration and performance remain separate questions.

## How it works

- Assign intrabar volume by open/close direction, then prior-close direction for dojis, then carry last polarity; sum signed volume per chart bar.
- Build instant delta, EMA difference, RSI-centered momentum, ALMA-smoothed excess-volume and percentage balances, plus combined-state/marker summaries.
- Scale top/bottom candle extensions by delta share of volume relative to recent body size; save/expand divergence-channel levels until breached and renewed.
- Sign intrabar volume by close-open; flat body uses close-previous_intrabar_close then last polarity. Sum U,D;Bar Balance=U-D;Average Balance=EMA(U,n)-EMA(D,n),caller n/LTF. Initial polarity,auto-LTF,ALMA,markers/momentum excluded.

## Outputs and intended use

- Inspect balance/price agreement, divergence-channel breaks and top/bottom EMA references; configure markers/alerts for the selected balance conditions.
- Usable scope: Historical raw/EMA directional-volume balances. Other advertised outputs remain subject to the listed missing information.

## Parameters and stated settings

- Five balances are documented. Default top/bottom sizing uses average candle body over 100 bars; discrepancy background flags more than 1% intrabar/chart volume mismatch.
- Divergence-channel defaults use open/close levels and close breaches; balance/EMA periods and intrabar precision are configurable.

## Failure modes and caveats

- Intrabar resolution trades precision for history; delta remains a price-direction proxy. Realtime values update and historical feed/start changes can recalculate; source says markers/alerts appear at close.

## Missing information and implementation boundary

- Full period defaults, ALMA settings, marker rules, exact LTF mapping and momentum-sign wording require code confirmation.

CVD Chart maps cumulative or raw intrabar volume delta onto the price pane in reset-defined zones. - Classify intrabar volumes by candle direction with prior-close/last-polarity fallbacks, sum up minus down and optionally accumulate until reset.
- Reset by none, fixed/stepped higher timeframe, clock time, regular-session start or selected trend-indicator change.
- Scale line/histogram zones to price ranges, offset beneath price and annotate extrema/values; color simple candle/delta polarity disagreements as divergences.
- Intrabar volume sign uses body,prior-close,last-polarity fallback. DV=U-D;CVD accumulates DV with no reset or resets at caller fixed-timeframe boundaries,including current bar after reset. Initial polarity/zero volume and trend resets/scaling remain limitations.

- Fixed intrabar targets are approximately 12/24/50/100/250; ten precision options and configurable Zone Height/labels/tooltips are described.
- Stepped resets map subminute to hourly, below three hours to daily, through twelve hours to weekly, below weekly to monthly and weekly-or-higher to annual.
